summary: A linguist, Nikolai Anderson studied under Leo Meyer at the University of Tartu (Cand. Phil.). He served as Oberlehrer für alte Sprachen at Minsk Gymnasium (1872–1894) and extraordinary Professor of Finno-Ugric at Kazan State University (1894–1905).

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Nikolai Maksimovich Goldberg studied at Heidelberg University (1910–1912). His posts included the Institute of History (1938) and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1943).

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and Alexander von Rospatt, later holding a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Linguist Nikolai Trubetzkoy studied at Moscow State University under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Southern Federal University (1918–1920), Sofia University (1920–1922), and the University of Vienna starting in 1922.

Nikolaj Dmitrievič Andreev worked in linguistics, Indology, and computational linguistics after graduating from Saint Petersburg State University. He worked at Leningrad State University's Experimental Laboratory of Machine Translation (1959–1965) and the Institute for Linguistic Studies (1965; ~1972–1997).

Nikolaus Delius worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Berlin under Franz Bopp and at Bonn under A. W. von Schlegel and Christian Lassen. After habilitating at Bonn, he served as Professor of English there from 1855 to 1880.

Nikolay Astakhaev, active in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy, studied at Buryat State University (2005–2008). He later worked at the Irkutsk Institute of Educators Training (2012–2015) and Yandex's Novosibirsk office (2015).

Working in Indology and linguistics, Nikolay Ivanovich Korolev studied at the Institute of Asian and African Studies at Moscow State University (~1953–1958). In 1958, he became a research scholar at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Linguist Nils Holmer studied at Lund University and Charles University. He served as Privatdozent of Celtic and Indo-European at Uppsala University in 1941 and was Professor of Linguistics at Lund University from 1949 to 1969.

Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at Lund University. He taught at Lunds privata elementarskola (1887–1919) and was Professor of Sanskrit and comparative Indo-European linguistics at Lund University (1898–1920).

Nils Simonsson specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics, studying at Uppsala, Paris, and Oslo. He served as Professor of Indian languages and literature at the University of Oslo (1963–1975) and Professor of Sanskrit at Uppsala University (1976–1985).
Nima Repper is an Indology scholar who holds an appointment as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Nimethri Gunasekara works in Buddhist studies and psychology. She served as a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Kelaniya (2024) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies as a psychologist and mindfulness trainer (attested 2026).

Nina Mirnig works in Indology and religious studies, having completed doctoral studies under Alexis Sanderson. She has held posts at the University of Groningen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, IKGA, and the University of Vienna.

Ninian Smart worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, completing a D.Phil. at Oxford. He was Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (1967–1989) and Professor in the Comparative Study of Religions at UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Historian and Indologist Nira Wickramasinghe studied at Paris-Sorbonne and earned her D.Phil. at Oxford. She was Professor of History and International Relations at the University of Colombo (1990–2009) before becoming Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University (2010).

Indologist Nirajan Kafle completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop. He has held positions at the Nepal Research Centre, Leiden University, the University of Naples 'L'Orientale', and Ashoka University (2023).

An archaeologist and Indologist, Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti studied at Calcutta and Cambridge under Edward James Rapson. He served as Government Epigraphist for India and was Director General of Archaeology in India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1948–1950).

Nirbhay N. Singh works in religious studies and psychiatry. He has held professorial posts at Virginia Commonwealth University and Augusta University, and served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies.
Nirmal C. Sinha served as Editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology, attested in 1978 and 1988.
